correctness.rationale: All pair classes are explicitly and exhaustively checked: center-to-shell, distinct shells, same shell, shell-to-outside, center-to-outside, outside-to-outside. The ultrametric identity \(d(x,y)=\max\{d(m,x),d(m,y)\}\) for distinct radii and the within-shell bound establish the lengths. The trunk \(H(t)\) is strictly increasing; each shell dendrogram has nonnegative edges and the required leaf height \(L(t)\). The rooted-tree edge-flow formula for optimal transport proves the equality for all probability weights and all centers. The checker independently verifies all pair costs and two independently solved LPs in 3,960 generated instances, and exhibits a four-point non-ultrametric obstruction. The general proof does not depend on the finite tests.

value.rationale: The new metric of McCabe–Perea is a natural stability invariant for weighted topology/nerve constructions. On every finite ultrametric, the theorem converts an outer maximum of inner transportation linear programs into exact explicit tree-cut sums for all weights and all scales, exposing its hierarchical geometry and supporting exact repeated comparisons without transport optimization. This is a structural theorem for a broad class, not an isolated small table or normalization. The non-ultrametric four-point obstruction shows the special hypothesis matters.
